suggestion: Snapshot the official NFL injury report every Tuesday to Saturday and store each snapshot in git
options: A) Manual daily copy; B) Scheduled GitHub Action that saves the page; C) Defer
pros: A: no tooling. B: builds history for designation drift. C: no history
cons: A: error-prone. B: needs an allowed fetch host and review of NFL terms. C: no data later

suggestion: Pull official team depth charts for all 32 teams each week to build starter and backup maps
options: A) Team pages on nfl.com; B) Third-party depth chart site (not official, would need flagging); C) Skip depth analysis
pros: A: official. B: broader coverage but unverified. C: no backup analysis
cons: A: slower to build. B: cannot be verified line by line. C: requirement unmet

suggestion: Set validation gates with numeric thresholds before any strategy is tested (minimum bets, seasons, out-of-sample share)
options: A) Conservative: 500+ graded bets over 3+ seasons; B) Moderate: 300+ bets over 2 seasons; C) User-defined
pros: A: fewer false positives. B: faster. C: user control
cons: A: slower. B: more luck risk. C: needs a decision first

suggestion: Pre-register every hypothesis in a committed file with a timestamp before any backtest
options: A) Git commit before testing; B) Registry file only; C) None
pros: A: strongest anti-luck control. B: weaker. C: highest luck risk
cons: A: extra steps. B: easy to edit after results. C: not recommended

suggestion: Control for multiple comparisons when many strategies are tested
options: A) Bonferroni; B) Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR); C) Holdout season only
pros: A: strict. B: balanced. C: simple
cons: A: may reject real edges. B: needs more tests. C: uses the data once

suggestion: Rank strategies by out-of-sample closing-line value first, then ROI; show ROI only after gates pass
options: A) CLV first; B) ROI first; C) Risk-adjusted score
pros: A: measures skill rather than luck. B: easy to read. C: accounts for variance
cons: A: needs closing lines. B: rewards variance. C: harder to explain

suggestion: Reward design: non-monetary points and public badges for strategies that pass all gates
options: A) Points only; B) Public badges; C) No rewards
pros: A: no gambling mechanics. B: visible recognition. C: simplest
cons: A: less motivation. B: may encourage gaming. C: no incentive

suggestion: Restrict the project to research and analysis only, with no wagering, until a legal review is complete
options: A) Research only; B) Research and paper-trading only; C) Continue as planned
pros: A: lowest legal risk. B: tests strategies without money. C: highest risk for a Japan-based user
cons: A: no betting feedback. B: still gambling-related to review. C: not recommended before legal review

suggestion: Add an automated link checker and data-validation step to CI before each deploy
options: A) GitHub Action; B) Manual script run; C) None
pros: A: catches broken links on each change. B: depends on memory. C: risk of broken pages
cons: A: small setup effort. B: not automatic. C: higher risk

suggestion: Add a LICENSE file and a .gitignore before adding more data
options: A) Add a license chosen by the user; B) Leave unlicensed; C) Other
pros: A: clarity for reuse. B: default all-rights-reserved. C: depends
cons: A: user must choose. B: unclear reuse. C: depends
